sections.title: Page 5

summary.text: The preface explains that the guidelines highlight key principles for accelerating immunization programmes and will need regular updating. It states that they supplement, rather than replace, the EPI training materials and mentions a related UNICEF issue paper.

sections.extract: PREFACE L'objet des présentes directives est de mettre en lumière certains grands principes relatifs à l'accélération du programme. Comme les politiques en matière de vaccination évoluent rapidement, il conviendra d'actualiser et de réviser ces direc- tives chaque fois que cela sera nécessaire, Celle-ci complètent, mais ne remplacent pas, les matériels didactiques préparés par le Programme élargi de vaccination

sections.title: Page 7

summary.text: Opens the introduction, noting that with 1990 approaching only about a third of children in developing countries outside China receive a third dose of polio and DTP vaccines. It argues that political will to raise coverage is not hard to mobilize, as leaders welcome promises of protecting children cheaply.

sections.extract: 1. INTRODUCTION > 1990 approche à grands pas et si la couverture vaccinale dans le monde est en progression, elle n'en demeure pas moins tout à fait insuffisante. summary.text: Explains vaccine timing, with measles vaccine delayed to nine months, oral polio from birth and DTP from six weeks, and advises a minimum four-week interval between doses. It stresses registering and tracking newborns so that older at-risk children cease to be a problem.

summary.text: Opens the section on planning acceleration, stressing that plans must cover at least three years rather than a single immunization day. It recommends joint national and international technical reviews of one to three weeks to draw up an acceleration plan.

summary.text: Describes the careful planning needed for social mobilization, with messages and channels chosen for each group whose support is needed. It warns that vaccine supplies require long lead times, citing a case where a promised delivery was met only by diverting vaccines from other countries.

sections.extract: -12- Le côté du programme qui intéresse le public, ou les utilisateurs, nécessite une planification méticuleuse et des délais importants. Il y a loin entre une mobilisation sociale efficace et l'envoi à l'avance d'une personne chargée d'annoncer au voisinage à l'aide d'un haut-parleur qu'une séance de vaccination va avoir lieu. L'information nécessaire et les messages doivent être analysés pour chacun des groupes

summary.text: Explains that successful national immunization days need careful planning of vaccine supply, volunteer training and publicity, plus personal involvement of top political leaders. It warns of risks, chiefly sustainability, and that mass efforts tend to reach older children rather than the youngest at greatest risk.

sections.title: Page 28

summary.text: The conclusion says acceleration should improve the quality of existing services, with training, supervision and community participation, and that national days must support lasting services. It begins a checklist of requirements, such as a schedule allowing three doses at four-week intervals.

sections.title: Page 29

summary.text: Continues the checklist of features that make acceleration compatible with routine services, such as record systems, compatible cold-chain equipment and volunteers coordinated with health staff. It ends with evaluating coverage separately for children under 12 months.

sections.extract: - 29 - Utilisation ou adoption de dossiers et d'un système d'enregistrement pouvant être utilisé par les services de santé ordinaires. Commande de matériel de chaîne du froid, de fournitures et de moyens de transport s'harmonisant avec les matériels déjà utilisés dans les services de santé. Organisation d'une structure bénévole en coordination avec les personnels de santé permanents et les services de santé.

sections.title: Page 30

summary.text: Completes the checklist with evaluating impact on polio, measles and neonatal tetanus and planning evaluation in advance, and urges that acceleration strengthen health infrastructure.

sections.extract: - 30 - Evaluation de l'impact du programme sous l'angle de la réduction du taux d'inci- dence des maladies cibles, l'accent por- tant en particulier sur la poliomyélite, la rougeole et le tétanos néonatal.
